question: A solution of a weak acid and its salt is called:
solution:
The correct answer is** Buffer solution.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__​​**

__
 
• A** buffer solution is an aqueous mixture of a weak acid **and either its conjugate base or base itself. When a modest amount of a strong acid and base is introduced to it, the pH hardly changes at all.
 
• The two main categories of the buffer are alkaline and acidic buffer solutions. Acidic buffers are solutions that contain a** weak acid and one of its salts and have a pH below 7.**
 
• To keep the** pH neutral or even slightly alkaline**, buffer solutions are employed in the production of many cosmetic and personal hygiene products. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​​**

 
• An** aqueous solution that has more OH- ions than H+ ions** is referred to as a basic solution. It is an aqueous solution with a pH higher than 7, in other words.
 
• The same** concentrations of hydrogen and hydroxide ions** are considered to be neutral solutions.
 
• Higher than that of pure water, **an acidic solution has a high concentration of hydrogen ions (H +start superscript). ​**
